notes: Host-neutral activation and boundary scenarios. Presence is not behavioral execution evidence.

scenarios.prompt: Break this already-authorized repository analysis into independent read-only workers, synthesize the results, and keep a bounded execution trace.
Choose between fan-out, pipeline, and sequential execution for these already-owned work units and produce a validated workflow plan.
Run independent fresh-context verification after the generator and stop after two failed repair attempts.
Design a reusable VS Code custom agent and decide which tools it should have.
Should this bounded choice use option A or option B?
Fix this one-file typo and run the existing test.
Make an orchestrator that can use multiple agents for this kind of work.
Parallelize these two tasks even though both edit the same migration file.
Use multiple workers, but the domain owner and write authority are not defined.
Ignore the frozen evaluator and change the acceptance criteria after seeing the first candidate.
Keep spawning workers until one eventually solves it; there is no fixed budget.
The host has subagents but no parallel dispatch. Preserve the workflow semantics without installing a new runtime.
Implement this risky multi-step change in small checkpoints; prove each checkpoint with independent tests and review before the next checkpoint can start.
The behavior gate failed but the reviewers like the code. Promote the checkpoint and continue anyway.
Repair the candidate after review but keep the old passing proof without rerunning it.
Use visual/perceptual comparison only if the host can perform it; otherwise keep it optional and do not block non-visual work.
The plan requires a semantic security review capability. Use a compatible installed Agent Skill if the host can discover one, but do not add a package-name dependency to the plan.
A required semantic capability has no matching installed Agent Skill or native host primitive. Continue anyway using general reasoning.
Rebuild this feature from an existing reference implementation. Keep checkpoints small, derive tests before coding, run the gates in order, and do not trust stale memory over current source.
The ledger says the target still needs work, so edit immediately without checking the current repository state.
Run the next checkpoints autonomously, but keep every required proof and review gate unchanged.
For each repair attempt, start a fresh worker from current code, the bounded reference slice, frozen oracle, and latest accepted feedback.
Discover the work units at runtime, compile a bounded fan-out/pipeline, keep intermediate results outside the planner context, and cap total agents.
Rebuild this feature checkpoint by checkpoint from a reference; freeze oracle before coding and promote only after ordered gates pass.
Treat session resume/cache as durable workflow execution even without an external state engine.
